title: Library construction and imaging for high-throughput image-based screening using multiplexed FISH
protocol: Mix all barcode construction oligonucleotides listed in Table 1 in water to a final concentration of 100 nM each.
Mix 16 µL of the above oligonucleotide mixture, 2 µL T4 ligase buffer, and 2 µL PNK in a PCR tube.
Incubate this mixture at 37 °C for 30 minutes to phosphorylate any oligonucleotides that may have lost the phosphorylation provided during synthesis.
Incubate the mixture at 65 °C for 20 minutes to heat inactive the PNK.
Add 1 µL T4 ligase (NEB, M0202S) to this mixture and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature to ligate oligonucleotides forming DNA templates for RNA barcodes.
Dilute the ligation product 10-fold into water.

Mix 5 µL of diluted ligation product with 25 µL Phusion 2X master mix, 2.5 µL 20X EvaGreen, and barcode amplification primers to a final concentration each of 0.5 µM, adding water to reach a total volume of 50 µL.
PCR amplify this reaction via limited cycle PCR.
Gel purify the PCR product using the Zymoclean DNA recovery kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the gel-purified product into 20 µL water.
PCR amplify 50 μL of the specific backbone vector.
Gel purify the amplified backbone vector (as in previous steps).
Elute the gel-purified backbone vector in 20 μL water.
Mix 5 µL of the gel-purified barcode ligation product with 5 µL of the gel-purified barcode expression backbone.
Add 10 µL HiFi DNA assembly master mix to the mixture.
Incubate the mixture for 1 hour at 50 °C.
Purify the fused product using the Zymo DNA clean and concentrator kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Elute the purified plasmid library with 6 μL water.
Mix assembled plasmids with 10 µL of electrocompetent E. coli on ice.
Transfer the mixture into an electroporation cuvette on ice.
Electroporate using an Amaxa Nucleofector II set to bacteria program 3.
Immediately add 1 mL SOC to the electroporated cells.
Transfer the mixture into a 14 mL culture tube.
Incubate at 37 °C on a shaker for one hour.
Dilute this culture into 50 mL of LB supplemented with 0.1 mg/mL carbenicillin in a sterile, beveled 250 mL flask.
Place the diluted culture on the shaker at 37 °C overnight to allow cells which have taken up a plasmid to grow.
Miniprep the overnight culture using the Zyppy plasmid miniprep kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the final barcode plasmid library into 30 μL Zymo elution buffer.
Store the eluted plasmid library at -20 °C until needed.

Amplify and gel purify the corresponding halves of the barcode plasmid library and an existing genetic variant library by limited-cycle PCR using the appropriate barcode-genetic-variant-fusion primers.
Mix 5 μL of each purified plasmid library fragment with 10 μL HiFi DNA assembly master mix.
Incubate for 1 hour at 50 °C to assemble these PCR fragments.
Purify the resulting plasmids using the Zymo DNA clean and concentrator kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the plasmid library into 6 μL of water.
Transform this library into electrocompetent E. coli.
Re-isolate this plasmid library via plasmid extraction as described in 1.10 – 1.12.
Dilute this plasmid library to a defined concentration of 100 pg/μL in water.
Re-electroporate the diluted plasmid library into E. coli (as in 1.10 – 1.12).
Measure the OD600 of the overnight culture.
Dilute the culture to a concentration of ~1000 cells/μL using the conversion of 800 million cells per 1 unit of OD600.

Inoculate 2 mL of LB containing 0.1 mg/mL carbenicillin with a volume of culture corresponding to the desired library size (typically at most 10% of the expected number of unique barcodes in the original barcode library).
Incubate at 37 °C overnight on a shaker to grow this culture to saturation.
Miniprep 600 μL of the overnight culture.
Elute the miniprepped DNA into 30 μL Zymo elution buffer.
Store the plasmid library at -20°C for later use in next-generation sequencing.
Mix the remaining overnight culture with an equal volume of 50% glycerol to archive E. coli containing the barcoded genetic-variant library.
Separate the mixed culture-glycerol solution into 100 μL single-use aliquots.
Store the aliquoted mixture at -80°C for long-term storage.
Dilute the barcoded genetic variant plasmid library tenfold in water.
Amplify 5 μL of this dilution via limited cycle PCR using Illumina-sequencing-adaptor primers.
Gel purify the amplified product as previously described.
Elute the gel-purified product in 200 μL of water.
Repeat amplification using different primer sets for sequencing the desired region.
Amplify and gel purify 5 μL of product using primers at a reduced concentration of 0.05 µM.
Elute the amplified product into 10 μL water.
Quantify the concentration of eluted product using the Qubit fluorimeter.
Dilute the quantified product to 4 nM in water.
Sequence molecules following the MiSeq protocol from Illumina.
Construct barcode to genetic variant look-up table by grouping sequencing reads by UMI and assigning the most frequently occurring barcode and gene variant seen for that UMI.
Thaw a 100 μL aliquot of barcoded genetic-variant library to room temperature.
Dilute the thawed library into 2 mL LB supplemented with 0.1 mg/mL carbenicillin.
Incubate diluted library on shaker at 37 °C for 3 hours to allow cells to grow.
Add 20 µL of chloramphenicol to the culture to achieve a final concentration of 34 µg/mL.
Incubate the culture at 37 °C for an additional 3 hours.
Coat an imaging coverslip with 1% PEI in water for 30 minutes.
Wash the coverslip once in PBS.
Dry the coverslip by removing the PBS.
Dilute the above culture 10-fold into PBS.
Pour the diluted culture onto the coated coverslip.
Spin the petri dish in a centrifuge at 100g for 5 minutes to force E. coli cells to lie flat on the surface of the coverslip.
Wash the coverslip once with PBS.
Prepare aliquots of water, PBS, 2X SSC, and fixation buffer (80% v/v methanol and 20% v/v acetone).
Prepare an imaging buffer by mixing 50 mM TrisHCl pH 8, 10% w/v glucose, 2 mM Trolox, 0.5 mg/mL glucose oxidase, and 40 µg/mL catalase in 2X SSC.
Prepare a cleavage buffer consisting of 50 mM TCEP in 2X SSC.
Prepare a master hybridization mix containing 5% w/v dextran sulfate, 5% w/v ethylene carbonate, 0.05% w/v yeast tRNA, and 0.1% v/v Murine RNase inhibitor in 2X SSC.
Aliquot 1 mL of the hybridization master mix into each 15 mL falcon tube for each round of hybridization.
Add readout probes to a final concentration of 10 nM to each aliquot, as specified for determining bit values.
Load all buffers and hybridization mixes into the fluidics system.
Assemble the coverslip into the flow chamber according to manufacturer instructions.
Flow PBS into the chamber and place it on the microscope.
Proceed with high-resolution imaging protocol for phenotype measurement.
Fix the cells by washing the flow chamber with water.
Incubate the sample at room temperature for 30 minutes in the fixation buffer.
Wash the sample again with water.
Flow on the hybridization buffer containing the readout probes assigned to the first hybridization round.
Incubate the sample at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Flow the imaging buffer onto the sample.
Collect an image of each field-of-view when illuminated with 750-nm light.
Collect an image of each field-of-view when illuminated with 650-nm light.
Collect an image of each field-of-view when illuminated with 560-nm light.
Collect a brightfield image of the field-of-view for image alignment.
Repeat steps for as many fields of view as desired.
Flow the cleavage buffer onto the sample.
Incubate the sample for 15 minutes.
Flow 2XSSC onto the sample to remove residual cleavage buffer.
Repeat steps 3.5 to 3.12 for each round of hybridization.
Use integrated microscope and fluid handling software to automate imaging, fluid handling, and flow processes.
Correct inhomogeneities in illumination using flat-field correction determined by averaging fluorescence signals across multiple fields of view.
Align images from each round of imaging by maximizing cross-correlation of bright-field images.
Segment cells by determining closed boundaries after applying the Canny edge detection algorithm.
Calculate mean fluorescence intensity for each cell across all constituent pixels in each image.
Normalize intensity observed for each color channel and round by the mean intensity observed for that color channel and round across all fields of view.
Determine the ratio of fluorescence signal for the readout probe associated with a “0” signal to that for a “1” signal in each cell.
Select approximately 100 barcodes known to be present in the sample via next-generation sequencing.
Determine the frequency of detection of these barcodes as a function of bit-calling-threshold for each bit.
Choose the set of thresholds that maximize barcode detection frequency.
For each cell, determine the value of the measured barcode using the selected thresholds and “0”-to-“1” ratios.
Discard cells with barcodes assigned to multiple genetic variants based on next-generation sequencing data.
Discard cells with a “1” or “0” brightness below a given threshold to increase accuracy.
Group cells together that are expressing the same barcode to determine average properties of the measured phenotype.
